messages:
maya: quick sync — we just rolled back a canary deploy and noticed two things: 1) a new medium-high SAST finding surfaced in a vendored lib, and 2) terraform applied an RBAC tweak to the deployer SA that doesn't show in our audit view. i'm going to pause merges to main. thoughts? :warning:

jordan: ack. what did the RBAC change do exactly? partial perms or full role grant?

maya: looks like a new grant: `roles/compute.instanceAdmin` on the canary-project to `svc-deployer@redwood.iam`. no terraform drift PR — it was in a hotfix apply. audit logs for iam.setIamPolicy calls aren't showing up in the central audit bucket yet.

sam: oncall — i can grab the cloud audit stream. maya, can you file a ticket with the apply's tfplan/diff and the deploy run id? will preserve evidence. also suggest we freeze deployer SA tokens (short term) if we can't find the audit entries.

maya: filing now — JIRA REDWOOD-SEC-1428. adding tfplan and pipeline run id. putting DO-NOT-MERGE label on active PRs.

eli: from product side — what's the impact to customers? do we need a communications plan?

maya: no customer-facing impact yet; canary failed and auto-rolled back. still want to treat this as policy/forensics item.

jordan: regarding the SAST hit — it's in `vendor/oldparser` flagged for path traversal. looks like a new transitive version was pulled in. can we backfill which commit introduced it?

sam: running a quick `git bisect` on the lockfile now. also exporting logs — if anyone needs them: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evidence/tmp/REDWOOD-SEC-1428/ ./ --recursive` or for GCP `gsutil -m cp -r gs://redwood-audit/tmp/REDWOOD-SEC-1428 ./`

maya: two operational asks: (A) how to ensure the RBAC change is audited moving forward (we didn't get the iam write in central bucket), (B) safe process to rotate the deployer SA key if we need to revoke tokens without breaking pipelines.

jordan: (A) we should confirm organization-level audit config: enable "Admin Activity" for iam.* and export to central sink. if it's already enabled, maybe the sink filter dropped setIamPolicy; check filter and sink permissions. cmd to inspect GCP sink: `gcloud logging sinks describe redwood-audit-sink --project=infra-org`

jordan: (B) for key rotation: create a short-lived key, add to CI secrets in parallel, wait one CI run to pass, then revoke old key. don't delete the key until traffic uses the new one. we should document this in the deployer runbook.

sam: adding a temporary mitigation: add an inline IAM condition to the deployer role restricting to pipeline service account source IPs (if we have them) and add an expiration timestamp: helps limit blast radius while we investigate.

eli: can sec ops own the emergency rollback play? we need a clear SLO for time-to-rollback and evidence collection. dev should declare rollback window to avoid DB drift.

maya: propose a short playbook stub in the repo under `security/playbooks/emergency-rollback.md`. rough steps: 1) Pause PR merges, 2) Trigger canary rollback if not auto, 3) Snapshot db, 4) Export audit/log bundles to evidence bucket, 5) Rotate affected keys/tokens (staged), 6) Run full SAST on checkout, 7) Postmortem within 48h.

jordan: can we add a CI gate to block merges if the repo has new high SAST findings introduced in the PR? we've relied on the aggregated dashboard but need faster feedback. suggestion: a pre-merge job that runs `sast-scan --diff` and fails on new sev>=high.

maya: +1. also want a DAST quick smoke job against canary endpoints before promoting canary to prod. low budget scan but catches obvious regressions.

sam: for evidence preservation, run these commands asap (examples):
```
# export cloud audit entries (gcp)
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy" AND resource.type="project"' --limit 50 --format json > sec-1428-iam.json

# export recent terraform state and plan
terraform show -json > tfstate.json
cat tfplan.out > tfplan.txt
```

maya: i've uploaded sec-1428-iam.json and tf artifacts to `gs://redwood-evidence/REDWOOD-SEC-1428/` and linked them on the ticket.

eli: who will own the postmortem? need an owner for follow-ups (audit sink config, runbook updates, CI gates).

maya: i'll own immediate follow-ups (runbook + ticket triage). jordan take CI gate and scan diff job. sam own audit sink verification and evidence ingest. i'll loop in infra and compliance.

sec-bot: NOTE: Incident created — REDWOOD-SEC-1428. Pager duty notified to oncall rotation. Runbook template: https://wiki.internal.redwood/security/playbooks/emergency-rollback

jordan: one non-blocker but important: vendor dependency hygiene — add a weekly job to `dependabot` or `renovate` that runs SAST on upgraded deps and flags risky transitive upgrades.

maya: agreed. ok folks, next steps in the jira. i'll follow up here when audit sink status is confirmed. thanks. :thumbsup:
